target_game.audience_proxy: Broad casual audience, appealing to both male and female players across a wide age range (10-35) looking for quick, competitive bursts.
target_game.visual_style: Vibrant, minimalist 3D top-down with bright, solid colors.

game_fit_scores.rationale: This live-action "POV rushing home" hook shows zero gameplay and explicitly references a different title (Tetris Block Party), which is a hard friction — Paper.io 2's UA historically converts on fast, readable territory-capture gameplay loops, not lifestyle skits. The palette overlaps only on #FFD700 and the hoodie/bedroom aesthetic clashes with the bright, minimalist 3D top-down look. Audience skew (teen/young adult casual) is plausibly compatible, but the cluster is tiny (n=1, single advertiser) and unproven — only worth testing if reshot with Paper.io 2 gameplay swapped into the tablet, otherwise skip.

This is a Bus Jam / parking-puzzle satisfaction hook — its slow, deliberate "relax" pitch directly contradicts Paper.io 2's energetic, competitive arcade DNA, and the muted white/red palette clashes with the game's neon primaries. Mechanically there is no overlap: trail-drawing/territory capture cannot be faked into a grid-clearing puzzle without misleading-ad risk and poor IPM post-install. Only the casual broad audience loosely overlaps; recommend skipping this archetype and instead testing satisfying-territory-fill or near-miss tension hooks that stay native to the .io loop.

The "fail · in-game" hook is built around a hand-driven traffic/parking puzzle with collision fails — a fundamentally different mechanic from Paper.io 2's trail-drawing territory capture, so the gameplay shown would mislead users and tank IPM/retention. The muted gray/white/green palette also clashes hard with Paper.io's bright primary + neon accent identity, and there's no character or top-down arena read. Audience has partial overlap (broad casual puzzle players), but recommend NOT adapting this archetype as-is; if the team wants to test a "fail" hook, rebuild it natively around a near-miss trail crossing or a player getting cut off mid-capture.

Hard pass for Paper.io 2. The muted earth-tone palette (#4A5D6A, #8B7355, #2F3E46) and architectural cross-section storytelling are the polar opposite of the game's bright neon top-down territory grab — there is no plausible bridge from "secret bunker reveal" to drawing trails and capturing zones, so the hook would massively mis-set expectations and tank IPM/D1. Additionally the archetype is a single-creative cluster (327d old, velocity 0.092), so there's no market validation to justify the production cost of force-fitting it.

This is a live-action/3D-render slapstick skit borrowed from the Gardenscapes playbook — palette, character (real human + cat), and tone have zero overlap with Paper.io 2's bright, minimalist top-down arcade DNA. The hook also tells viewers nothing about drawing trails or capturing territory, so even if curiosity drives the click, install-to-engagement will collapse on a snackable .io loop. Skip unless you're willing to fund a custom shoot AND bolt on a clear gameplay payoff in seconds 3-6, which isn't justified by a single 380-day-old reference creative.

brief.title: POV: I Got Home and Opened Paper.io 2
brief.hook_3s: POV: backpack drops, phone unlocks, screen explodes with neon yellow territory swallowing the map.
scene_flow: 0-3s: Live-action POV — hand pushes open bedroom door, flops onto bed, phone lights up with Paper.io 2 icon glowing.
3-6s: Tap. Hard cut into the game — bright top-down arena, our yellow #FFD700 square bursts out of home base carving a clean trail.
6-10s: Quick montage of satisfying captures — sweeping a huge loop, slicing a cyan #00BFFF rival's trail, kill-feed pops, territory floods yellow.
10-13s: Greedy run across the map for the win — magenta #FF00FF rival closes in, last-second dodge, claim 80% of the board.
13-15s: Player on bed grins, phone tilts to camera showing victory screen, CTA slams in.
brief.visual_direction: Split-personality spot: gritty handheld live-action bookends (warm bedroom light, hoodie, tablet/phone POV) crashing into the hyper-clean Paper.io 2 world — vibrant minimalist 3D top-down, solid #FFD700 hero territory, #00BFFF and #FF00FF rivals, white grid floor. The contrast between messy real life and the crisp, high-contrast arcade arena IS the hook. Energetic competitive UI: progress bar, kill-feed flashes, coin pings. Cuts on the beat, punchy SFX, no filler frames.
brief.rationale: Voodoo's current Paper.io 2 rotation is 100% in-engine Unity/Admob gameplay cuts with no copy and no creator-style framing — this brief injects the trending live-action "POV rushing home" UGC hook the market scan flagged, but fixes the archetype's fatal flaw by swapping in real Paper.io 2 gameplay on the phone instead of referencing a competitor title. UA team: ship this as the UGC/lifestyle top-of-funnel test against the existing pure-gameplay control, same audience, expect stronger thumb-stop on TikTok/Reels placements where lo-fi POV outperforms clean capture footage.

brief.title: Oddly Satisfying Territory Fill — ASMR Paper.io
brief.hook_3s: A neon-yellow square slowly carves a perfect spiral into a deep blue grid — every snap of color triggers a crisp ASMR pop.
scene_flow: 0-3s: Top-down close-up of a tiny yellow cube tracing a clean magenta-edged trail across a pristine cyan board, ASMR 'snap' as the first chunk fills in.
3-7s: Camera pulls back slightly — player carves bigger and bigger loops, each fill triggering a satisfying color-pop and percentage counter ticking up (12%… 28%… 47%).
7-11s: Tension beat: a red enemy creeps toward the trail, near-miss dodge, then player loops back and ENGULFS the enemy's whole territory in one sweep — explosion of magenta confetti.
11-14s: Board is now 90% gold, percentage hits 100%, screen flashes with 'SO SATISFYING' overlay and a clean victory chime.
14-15s: CTA card with Paper.io 2 logo and 'Play Free' button pulse.
brief.visual_direction: Lean fully into Paper.io 2's vibrant minimalist 3D top-down DNA: glossy solid-color territories with soft drop shadows, the gold (#FFD700) player against deep cyan (#00BFFF) board, magenta (#FF00FF) trail edges that glow on contact. Slow, deliberate camera with micro-zooms on each fill — borrow the satisfying 'reveal' rhythm from the bus-jam archetype but expressed through territory paint, not grid-clearing. Crisp ASMR sound design (paper crinkles, soft pops, click of the percentage counter) replaces voiceover. No UI clutter — let the colors breathe.
brief.rationale: Voodoo's current Paper.io 2 rotation is all unlabeled Unity/Admob playables and videos with no satisfaction/ASMR angle — they're missing the trending 'oddly satisfying' hook that's dominating casual feeds. This brief adapts the satisfaction archetype natively (territory paint instead of bus-jam) so it stays truthful to the install experience while capturing a fresh emotional lane. UA should test against the existing competitive/tension creatives to see if calm-satisfying outperforms on female 25-35 and broad casual segments.
